bug_semantics: The JavaScript Code node executes user code in the task-runner Node VM with host objects injected into the sandbox. `$input.constructor.constructor.prototype` is the host Function.prototype. The freeze loop only froze prototypes with `typeof === 'object'`, but `typeof Function.prototype === 'function'`, so that prototype stayed mutable. An authenticated user who can create and execute workflows can pollute Function.prototype, recover host globalThis, and complete a sandbox escape when allowlisted imports (NODE_FUNCTION_ALLOW_BUILTIN / NODE_FUNCTION_ALLOW_EXTERNAL) supply gadgets. CWE-1321. Patched in 1.123.69, 2.33.4, and 2.34.1 by freezing function-typed prototypes as well (`isFreezable` = object or function).
flaw_origin: Not an original omission of all prototype freezing. Commit bdf266cf55032d05641b20dce8804412dc93b6d5 (2025-01-15, #12588) froze every globalThis function's `.prototype` unconditionally, which does freeze Function.prototype (Function is the second function-valued global). The first public write of the defective skip is squash 562d867483e871b0f1e31776252e23bd721df75b (`chore: Bundle 2026-W7`, #26214, cherry-picked from inaccessible n8n-private#19): it replaced `Object.freeze(fn.prototype)` with `if (typeof fn.prototype === 'object') Object.freeze(fn.prototype)`. That guard was meant to skip undefined prototypes (parseInt etc.) but also skipped Function.prototype. Immediate parent 3f02194f6d17bc2b8c682e38a891413e48cbd0c1 still has the unconditional freeze and lacks the type-guard.
